newsitem.title: CANADA: Aber says A418 grade variation expected. [CORRECTED 21:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Aber says A418 grade variation expected. [CORRECTED 21:07 GMT]

text.p: Aber Resources Ltd said on Thursday that grade variation in a bulk sample from the A418 kimberlite pipe on its Diavik diamond property was not surprsing and it was unclear whether diamond values would vary in different areas of the pipe.
Aber earlier announced partial results from processing of more than 3,000 tonnes from the A418 kimberlite pipe at Diavik in Canada's Northwest Territories.

Processing of 1,490 tonnes yielded a grade of 2.8 carats a tonne. A 306-tonne part of that sample had a grade of 6.2 carats a tonne and is believed to be similar to material at the upper part of the pipe (corrects to make clear the 306 tonnes did not come from the upper part of the pipe).
Aber spokesman Alan Bayless said the pipe's official grade estimate remained at 4.0 carats a tonne because this was representative of the pipe as a whole.

Because of technical and time limitations, the A418 bulk sample was not taken from all areas of the pipe, Bayless said. The pipe was already known to have internal variations in rock character and grade.
The main purpose of the bulk sampling was to obtain a large number of diamonds for valuation and the grade of the sample was not a significant factor, Bayless said.

Aber is unsure whether there will be a variation in values for diamonds taken from different parts of the pipe. An Antwerp diamond expert will evaluate 4,217 carats from the bulk sample and valuations will be released before June 25.

Aber expected to disclose a more precise resource estimate for the A418 pipe in the late summer or early autumn, Bayless said. Its current estimate is nine million tonnes of ore grading 4.0 carats a tonne.
Aber shares were up 1.20 to 20.50 in Toronto. The update report probably reassured investors that the project was progressing well, Bayless said.
A plan to develop at diamond mine at the Diavik property, 60 percent controlled by RTZ Corp Plc, is expected to be submitted to regulatory authorities by the end of the year.
